STX.reasoning: 1. MACRO REGIME: Mixed-to-cautious. Iran missile escalation on May 4 reversed the May 1 risk-on narrative (Iran peace talks had briefly driven WTI -2% and S&P to record intraday high 7,230). Reported missile strikes on a US warship near Jask island have re-introduced Strait of Hormuz closure as a left-tail risk, pushing oil prices up and Dow futures lower. Fed held at 3.5%-3.75% with 4 dissents (most since 1992); Chair Powell transition May 15 adds policy uncertainty. No rate cuts signaled. Regime is NOT risk-on — wind is in the face of high-beta momentum names. 2. RELATIVE STRENGTH: STX is massively outperforming the market: ROC +24% (5d), +32.7% (10d), +71.8% (21d). Price is 58% above the 50-SMA, 138% above the 200-SMA, and has moved +140% YTD. Fundamental story is exceptional (Q3 FY26 revenue +44% YoY, nearline capacity allocated through 2027), but relative strength at this level signals a very late-stage move, not early rotation entry. 3. ASYMMETRIC R/R (FAILS 2:1 BAR): Entry at current price ~$738.73. Using nearest resistance at $751.01 (hourly pivot) as first target = +1.7% upside; Fib 1.272 ext = $799 = +8.2% upside. Stop placement is problematic: a proper stop below $697 (volume-confirmed hourly pivot, 3 tests) gives 5.7% downside, yielding 8.2%/5.7% = 1.44:1 — below the 2:1 minimum. A tighter stop at $727.20 (intraday pivot, 4 tests) achieves 5.25:1 asymmetry but is below the current hourly price ($738.73), meaning this requires a pullback entry that has not yet set up. Cannot enter at current price with acceptable R/R. 4. CAPITAL PRESERVATION FLAGS: Daily RSI-14 = 86.37, RSI-21 = 89.57 — extreme overbought. Bollinger pct_b = 1.126, price trading ABOVE the upper Bollinger band on daily. Z-score vs 50-day = 2.9 standard deviations. Most critically: hourly OBV is diverging bearishly from price (OBV trend down while price made new highs), with hourly relative volume only 0.54x — the latest push to $738-751 is on declining volume, a classic distribution warning. LESSONS FLAG: Prior trade loss (NVDA, Apr 30) explicitly cited stop-out 'amid stretched macro (RSI 81-87) with no bullish confirmation candle.' STX RSI is 86-90, higher than NVDA's when that trade failed. Do not repeat same stretched-RSI entry in a mixed macro regime. VERDICT: STX fundamental thesis (HDD duopoly, nearline supercycle) is intact and durable, but the current entry is a pass. Wait for pullback to $700-727 zone where R/R improves to 2:1+ and RSI resets toward 60-70 before re-engaging.

WDC.reasoning: 1. MACRO REGIME: Mixed-to-cautious (same as STX — HDD duopoly shares identical macro exposure). Iran escalation on May 4 reversed the prior risk-on posture; Strait of Hormuz closure is a left-tail scenario; Fed on hold with policy transition risk May 15. AI capex supercycle remains the fundamental driver for HDD demand (hyperscale bookings intact), but macro backdrop introduces headline risk that could reset these high-multiple momentum names. 2. RELATIVE STRENGTH: WDC is outperforming the broad market — ROC +6.8% (5d), +15.8% (10d), +44.9% (21d) — but meaningfully LESS stretched than STX (+24%/+32.7%/+71.8% comparable). WDC Z-score vs 50-day = 2.13 vs STX's 2.9; daily Bollinger pct_b = 0.90 (near but NOT above upper band, unlike STX). WDC's hourly RSI-21 = 65.74 (not overbought) vs STX's 77.42. WDC is in healthier technical shape — it's outperforming but not parabolic. Hourly OBV trend is UP and NOT diverging from price (STX has bearish OBV divergence). Daily institutional accumulation is clear: 2.08x relative volume on May 1 with OBV trend up and 10d volume bias up. 3. ASYMMETRIC R/R (MARGINALLY BELOW 2:1 THRESHOLD): Entry at ~$442.36 (current hourly price). Target: Daily Fib 1.272 extension at $500.36 = +13.1% upside. Stop: Hourly Fib 61.8% retracement at $414.51 = -6.3% downside. Asymmetry: 13.1%/6.3% = 2.08:1 — barely clears the 2:1 bar but is below the preferred 3:1+. Nearest resistance $446.62 (6 hourly tests, volume confirmed) acts as first hurdle and adds friction before the target. In a risk-on regime this would be a marginal bullish; in the current mixed-to-cautious regime the 2.08:1 asymmetry is insufficient margin of safety. 4. CAPITAL PRESERVATION FLAGS: Daily RSI-14 = 83.22 — overbought but less extreme than STX. At ~38x trailing P/E, WDC is richly valued; rate-driven multiple compression is a real risk if Iran escalation extends inflation expectations. Hourly ADX = 21.21 (moderate trend strength vs STX's 52.58), suggesting the trend may be cooling. No earnings catalyst in the immediate window. VERDICT: WDC is technically healthier than STX (lower RSI, Z-score below 2.5, OBV confirming, strong institutional volume) and the fundamental thesis (HDD duopoly, 2026 capacity fully booked) is intact. However, the macro regime is mixed-to-cautious, R/R is only 2.08:1, and we are entering — not early in — the sector's relative strength uptrend. Prefer waiting for a pullback to the $414-422 zone (hourly Fib 61.8% to $422 intraday support) where entry improves to approximately 3:1 R/R ($422 entry, $493 target, $396 stop = 16.8%/6.2% = 2.7:1 or better) before engaging. Stand aside until the setup improves or macro clears.
